target_customer: Technical distributors and manufacturers in HVAC, plumbing, electrical, building materials and industrial supplies
problem: Sales teams manually read emails, PDFs, scans and tenders, match each line to a product and key it into the ERP, so quotes take days. Mercura automates this with human review.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for quote and order processing integrated with the customer ERP
product_category: Vertical AI for quoting and order entry

founders.name: Lukas Bock
founders.background_notes: YC page says he grew up in a family HVAC and plumbing business; Munich Startup says the business has existed over 115 years.

founders.name: Stefan Zheng
founders.background_notes: Worked on operations at 15 plus manufacturing plants per YC page.

founders.name: Sean Sdahl
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no details.

founders.name: Hai Dang
founders.background_notes: YC launch post names him a co-founder though he is not in the YC founders list.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs robust extraction from messy documents, product matching against large catalogs and ERP write back. Standard LLM engineering with hard data matching parts.

defensibility.rationale: Catalog matching tuned per customer and ERP integrations create switching costs. Underlying models are widely available.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later sources show Prokeep launching AI quoting for distributors in February 2026 and Conga buying the PROS B2B unit in 2026, so adjacent players moved after the batch. No acquisition of Mercura found.

market_need_then: Distributor sales teams handle high volumes of unstructured requests. The company cites customers cutting quote time from 2 days to 2 hours (self reported) and the YC pitch is quotes in minutes not days.

identity.visual_style: Enterprise B2B site with named customer case studies and ISO 27001 badge
identity.voice_and_tone: Trade industry focused, emphasises craftsmanship heritage of the CEO family

branding.brand_signature: CEO's multi generation trades family story

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand itself. Heritage story is told by the company but evidence of recognition is thin.

outcome_analysis: Mercura is active. A Munich team with an insider CEO from the trades built an AI quoting product, was profitable before raising any outside capital per company information, and announced a seed of about 1.8M euros in January 2026 from TQ Ventures and SignalFire. It claims 80 plus customers in 20 plus countries. The open question is whether it can scale against ERP and CPQ vendors that moved into AI quoting in 2026.
notes: Seed amount: Munich Startup says more than 1.8M euros (about 2.1M USD) dated 2026-01-07; a late December 2025 date appears on aggregators. Aggregator totals of 500K and 2.6M conflict. YC page says founded 2024. No competitor with sources dated near the 2025 batch was found; Prokeep (2026) and Distro are undated or later. Sean Sdahl and Hai Dang have thin sourcing.
